definitions.gloss: to surface; to rise to the surface
definitions.explanation: To come up from below the surface of water or another medium. Used for submarines, divers, or objects rising through liquid.

definitions.gloss: to emerge; to come to light; to come to the fore
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, for issues, candidates, or possibilities to emerge or become apparent. Common in news and formal contexts.

examples.japanese: {潜水艦|せんすいかん}が{浮上|ふじょう}した。
ダイバーがゆっくりと{海面|かいめん}に{浮上|ふじょう}した。
examples.english: The diver slowly rose to the surface of the sea.

examples.japanese: {沈没船|ちんぼつせん}の{引|ひ}き{上|あ}げ{作業|さぎょう}で、{船体|せんたい}がようやく{浮上|ふじょう}した。
examples.english: The hull finally surfaced during the salvage operation for the sunken ship.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{問題|もんだい}が{浮上|ふじょう}した。
examples.english: A new problem has come to light.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{名前|なまえ}が{次期|じき}{社長|しゃちょう}の{候補|こうほ}として{浮上|ふじょう}した。
examples.english: His name emerged as a candidate for the next company president.

examples.japanese: {調査|ちょうさ}が{進|すす}むにつれて、{新|あたら}たな{疑惑|ぎわく}が{次々|つぎつぎ}と{浮上|ふじょう}している。
examples.english: As the investigation progresses, new suspicions are coming to light one after another.

notes:
Combines {浮|う}く (to float) and {上|じょう} (upward). The literal sense describes physical rising to a surface; the figurative sense is extremely common in news reporting and formal discussion for issues, names, or facts becoming apparent.

USAGE:
The figurative sense (sense 2) is more frequently encountered in daily life than the literal sense. It often appears in news headlines and political reporting.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {問題|もんだい}が{浮上|ふじょう}する — a problem comes to light
- {疑惑|ぎわく}が{浮上|ふじょう}する — suspicion emerges
- {候補|こうほ}として{浮上|ふじょう}する — to emerge as a candidate
- {海面|かいめん}に{浮上|ふじょう}する — to rise to the sea surface

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {浮|う}かび{上|あ}がる — to float up; to come to mind; more colloquial and versatile
- {表面化|ひょうめんか}する — to come to the surface (figurative only); emphasizes something hidden becoming visible
